items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forrest, and Joe Benjamin.

ctx.x: Yes, we loved it. Because, there was no rehearsal. On the first night out, somebody would say in the dressing room, let’s play so and so and everybody would agree on it and then you go from there. And you play one fast tune, one medium tempo, then everybody would have a solo. Then you’d go to the piano player and tell him what key and what tune you wanted to play. And that would go on for ….let’s see, Coleman Hawkins, Roy Eldridge, Flip Phillips, Bill Harris. After that, have an intermission and Ella Fitzgerald.…

And then too, after that I got a band together in New York. I had Elvin Jones, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Forrest, and Joe Benjamin. I had a real good swinging band too, oh we were really doing it. I kept that band together for about six years.
When did you start with that band, start putting it together?

items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: When he was out on the road he’d always call. If I was available I got the job, if not he got someone else.

ctx.x: So after Tyree Glenn, then Henry Sweets Edison seems significant.

Oh yeah, Henry would come in and sub for Tyree and that’s how I got to know him. We got this job—that’s how he knew about me. When he was out on the road he’d always call. If I was available I got the job, if not he got someone else. That was 1957 with J.J. then we toured and went to Sweden from Kiruna to Gothenburg
Yeah we got that part. So who was in the Harry Sweets Edison band with you?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.

ctx.x: Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.
Oh, you had Elvin in that band?
